Senses.Note: Several early exchanges recur in multiple lamp compilations. Repeated recensions establish transmission, but the curated set does not count each recension as an independent event. Frozen-corpus concordance: 451 exact hits in 167 storage files representing 163 independent works.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰。情知汝罔措。僧欲進語。師曰。將謂老僧落伊古今。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (五燈會元). Ziman owns the exact clause in the complete case.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰。情知你見作家來。濟曰。特來禮拜和尚。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (五燈會元). Pingtian Puan owns the exact clause in the complete case.

Occurrences.Kwic: 且畢竟見何道理？莫在世尊良久處麼？情知你向者裏錯會。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Collected Ancient Cases explicitly attributes the comment to the named-but-unrostered Baizhang Le: he anticipates that the reader misconstrues the case at the Buddha's silence.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 百丈泐云 introduces the complete comment through 情知你向者裏錯會; the inherited Jingfu name was not the speaker.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧云：「情知。」師云：「猛虎不食伏肉。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Langting exchange: an unnamed monk replies 'I knew it'; Langting Ting answers that a fierce tiger does not eat prostrate flesh.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 僧云：情知 explicitly assigns the compact reply to the unnamed monk; Langting answers in the next marked turn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一僧曰：「也是一橛頭禪。」師曰：「情知你恁麼。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (石雨禪師法檀). Shiyu Mingfang owns the exact clause in the complete case.

Occurrences.Kwic: 被梁王指出照乘明珠問之，情知伊道個不識。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (宗鑑法林). Zhongfeng Mingben owns the exact clause in the complete case.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧喝，師打云：情知汝這一喝
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (百癡禪師語錄): Baichi Yuan is the exact headword utterer; complete-turn review: public interview rebukes a monk’s shout with an explicit “I knew you would make this shout”.

Senses.Explanation: As I knew, sure enough, or I knew it marks prior expectation or recognition of the other turn. Ziman says he knew the monk was at a loss; Pingtian Puan says he knew Linji had seen an adept; Baizhang Le anticipates the reader's misconstrual; Shiyu Mingfang and Baichi Yuan mark the response they expected; Zhongfeng Mingben predicts Bodhidharma's 'I don't know.' An unnamed monk also uses the compact reply himself. These grammatical placements describe recognition of an ensuing or just-given turn, not a separate faculty of feeling-knowledge.
